solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vicissitudes rarely encountered in Holland

definitions.meaning: changes of fortune, good times alternating with bad
the Netherlands is famously flat, so rises and falls in the land are seldom met there

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a playful, literal reading: hills and dips are rare in a flat country like Holland.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicissitudes are the shifting fortunes of life, the good spells and bad spells taken together.

clue.text: Upper-class chief Scotsman finds too good to be true

parts.note: the top person is the chief
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name, standing for any Scotsman

explanation.surface: A posh Scottish leader discovers that something is too good to be true.
explanation.definitionFit: Something idealistic and impossibly perfect is described as being of an ideal, unreachable world.

clue.text: South side, it's hot and humid

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: The south side of town is sweltering and muggy.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapour from boiling water is hot and moist, matching the description.

clue.text: The gin ran out — almost a disaster

indicators.note: out means the letters of the preceding words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The bottle of gin has been finished, which nearly counts as a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran out' looks like a phrase about the gin running dry; 'ran' is fodder and 'out' alone is the anagram signal on THE GIN RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape, where calamity was only just avoided, is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: Spot an ineffectual person

definitions.meaning: a spot of liquid, a single drop falling
a feeble, wet person is informally called this

explanation.definitionFit: Both a falling droplet and a weak, wishy-washy person share this informal word.

clue.text: Express desire but in an irresponsible way

parts.note: to express desire for something is to want it
but means only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A person voices a longing, but does so recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting recklessly or without regard for consequences is acting in a wild, unrestrained manner.

clue.text: Play in street to get drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A busker plays music in the street to earn enough for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a guitar casually by brushing the strings is this verb.

clue.text: Foreshadow an empty decanter?

definitions.meaning: to foreshadow is to be an omen of something to come
a decanter of fortified wine that has been finished has reached the end of its port

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as PORT END: the end of the port, which leaves the decanter empty.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to signal in advance, an omen of events to come.

clue.text: Proposal to provide public with running water

parts.note: something done in public view is overt
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a stretch of running water

explanation.surface: A plan to supply the population with running water from the mains.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening approach or offer to negotiate is called this, as in making peace overtures.

clue.text: Relation seen in public performance

indicators.note: seen in places the word for relation inside the word for public

parts.note: something public is open to all
a ratio is a numerical relation between two quantities

explanation.surface: A family member turns up at a public show.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance in the sense of a functioning or carrying out of a procedure is a synonym.

clue.text: Partygoer in right state

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: A clubber is in the proper frame of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes to wild all-night dance parties is called this informally.

clue.text: Resident at home, needing companion

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a mate is a companion or friend

explanation.surface: Someone who lives alone at home wants company.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in an institution such as a prison or hospital is one of its occupants.

clue.text: Force acquiring thousands by way of business

indicators.note: acquiring means the word for force takes in the thousands

parts.note: to coerce is to force
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so MM gives thousands

explanation.surface: Strong-arm tactics that net huge sums are used as a way of doing business.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying and selling, trade on a large scale, is a synonym for business.

clue.text: Fool that's popular, backing another fool

indicators.note: backing means the word for popular is turned round

parts.note: something in fashion is in
a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: One idiot who is popular supports another idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid or silly person is called this colloquially.

clue.text: Match-box trial

parts.note: a test is an international cricket match
a case is a box

explanation.surface: A box of matches is being put through its paces.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; 'Match-box' looks like one object but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action whose outcome sets a precedent, or any trial example, is called this.

clue.text: Nothing lost in getting every necessity provided

definitions.meaning: if nothing is lost, everything has been recovered
an old phrase in job adverts meaning board and lodging included with wages

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a dated British term for a servant's terms of employment with food and lodging thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: Wages with keep included were advertised with this phrase, meaning all needs supplied.

clue.text: Anticipation of what might be set for tea

indicators.note: might be suggests these letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A preview of what could be laid out at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance sample or early experience of something to come is anticipation of it.

clue.text: Elegant braid one may make

indicators.note: may make suggests the letters are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: Someone might fashion a stylish plait.
explanation.definitionFit: A suave, stylish and charming manner is described with this word.

clue.text: Patient had to give up work

definitions.meaning: patiently accepting of something one cannot change
having left one's job by formally quitting

explanation.definitionFit: Accepting fate without complaint, and having formally quit a post, share the one past-tense word.

clue.text: Politician, liar and cad needs to reform

indicators.note: reform means the letters are formed afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A dishonest, caddish politician ought to mend his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a reforming or left-leaning political party may be called this.

clue.text: Mourn death of George, King and Emperor, the night before

parts.note: R is from Rex, Latin for king
I is from Imperator, Latin for emperor
an eve is the evening before a special day

explanation.surface: People lament the passing of a royal George, who was both King and Emperor, on the previous evening.
explanation.walkthrough: George V and George VI signed as R I, King and Emperor of India.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel deep sorrow after someone dies is to lament their loss.

clue.text: It's the absolute end!

parts.note: an exclamation of exasperation, read literally as the furthest limit

explanation.definitionFit: The utmost limit or furthest point is the end at its absolute.

clue.text: This ruler won't give an inch

definitions.text: This ruler won't give an inch

parts.words: This ruler won't give an inch
parts.note: a ruler is a measuring stick marked in inches, but here a tyrant who never compromises

explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler who never concedes ground is the autocrat in charge.

clue.text: The regions are as follows

explanation.surface: The territories are listed below.
explanation.definitionFit: Zones, districts or parts of a territory are synonyms of regions.

clue.text: Sound sort of artist

indicators.note: sort means sort out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician is a particular kind of artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow channel of sea, another word for a channel between landmasses.

clue.text: Maturing drink in silver container

indicators.note: container means the silver symbol holds the drink inside it

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Spirits mellowing in a silver vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing older and mellowing, as wine or cheese does over time.

clue.text: American lawman given thanks for information

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney in the US
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A US prosecutor is thanked for passing on intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures are information.

clue.text: Class or form taking English

parts.note: a cast is a mould or form

explanation.surface: A school class or form is taking English lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social rank is a class.

clue.text: Water for a mother pig

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
swine is another word for pig

explanation.surface: Water is given to a sow with piglets.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam, the first man, had only water to drink, hence the humorous phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular old phrase for water as a drink, since the first man had nothing else.

clue.text: Go flat out to broadcast good golf score

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to spread it
an eagle is two under par on a hole

explanation.surface: Make an all-out effort to announce a fine round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie stretched flat with arms and legs extended is this verb.
